passages.provision_quote: On a semiannual basis in accordance with subdivision (b), a social media company shall submit to the Attorney General a terms of service report.
passages.note: The chaptered text imposes posting and semiannual reporting duties on large platforms, including whether their terms define Disinformation or misinformation, but requires no removal, labeling or any other treatment of false content.
passages.actor_quote: AB 587, Gabriel. Social media companies: terms of service.

rows.reasoning: Gabriel authored AB 587 (2021-2022), which adds a chapter titled Content Moderation Requirements for Internet Terms of Service and compels large platforms to post their terms and report to the Attorney General on categories including Disinformation or misinformation, enforced by civil penalties. That is a government mandate on platform content moderation, so it cuts against the rungs that would protect free speech online and prevent government censorship or ban any government involvement in content moderation decisions, but its operative sections are disclosure duties: nothing in them would legally require platforms to remove false information, require platforms to label false content, rather than remove it, or merely encourage voluntary standards for combating misinformation online. One transparency statute shows a side, not which of the regulatory rungs he holds.
